newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Oil bounces further on slimmer N.Sea supply.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Oil bounces further on slimmer N.Sea supply.

text.p: Oil prices confounded the bears again on Thursday as leaner North Sea crude supply in April gave extra mileage to Wednesday's bounce.
Brent crude oil futures in London for April delivery closed 28 cents up at $19.89 a barrel.
The contract, due to expire on Friday, briefly touched a high of $20.02, the highest since early February.

Shell Expro, the Shell/Exxon joint venture that runs the giant Brent system of fields in the British North Sea, said there would be around 16 percent less oil pumped ashore from their pipeline in April.
"It looks like the system has been undershooting production targets," said one crude trader.

Traders who track tanker liftings from Brent and the Forties and Flotta North Sea pipeline systems said that the April loading schedules that have been released so far show the market will be 120,000 barrels per day (bpd) down on supply from last month.
But many saw the shortfall in April North Sea supply, attributable to seasonal maintenance work, running counter to the larger picture of mounting world supply.
Norway, the largest producer in the North Sea and thus in Europe, saw its output increase to 3.17 million bpd in February despite rough seas, a Reuter survey of operators showed.
Rising crude output and recent mild weather that has slashed demand for heating oil in Europe and the United States has badly hit refiners' profits and prompted plants to cut output.
That has knocked 19 percent off Brent's value since January 1, ending a six-month rally that took prices to their highest levels in six years.

Brent had slipped below $19.00 early on Wednesday on the back of rising stocks on both sides of the Atlantic and a steady stream of tankers carrying unsold crude to the glutted refineries of the U.S. Gulf Coast.
